name: Brunsbüttel
title: Brunsbüttel Ship Thickness Measurement at the Kiel Canal
description: UTM in Brunsbüttel for tankers, gas carriers, bulk carriers and Kiel Canal traffic: ballast tank, deck, hold and piping gauging at the Elbehafen and canal.
h1: Thickness Gauging at Brunsbüttel for Tankers, Bulk Carriers and Kiel Canal Ships
intro: Brunsbüttel guards the western entrance to the Kiel Canal on the north bank of the Elbe, and its port serves an industrial belt of chemical, fertiliser and energy plants as well as ships waiting for the canal locks. Tankers and bulk carriers work cargo at the Elbehafen, a floating regasification unit feeds gas into the German grid, and canal traffic passes in a steady stream. Atlantis does not station anyone at Brunsbüttel; the technicians are sent from India to the vessel for each job.

highlights.h: Liquid and dry bulk at the Elbehafen
highlights.p: The Elbehafen, outside the canal locks on the tidal Elbe, handles liquid and dry bulk for the industrial park behind it. Tankers and bulk carriers lie there long enough for cargo work to leave room for ballast tank, hold and deck gauging.

highlights.h: Ships trading on into the Baltic
highlights.p: Ships using the Kiel Canal to reach the Baltic pass Brunsbüttel, and many of them trade into ice-covered waters in winter. When one of them works cargo at the Elbehafen, ice-belt plating, frames and bow structure can be measured before the season begins.

The oil harbour and the Ostermoor harbour lie on the canal itself and serve chemical and energy plants. Chemical and product tankers at these berths can have ballast tanks, deck lines and engine-room piping gauged within the terminal's safety rules.

port.h: Brunsbüttel, the Elbe and the canal locks
p: Brunsbüttel lies on the north bank of the Lower Elbe in Schleswig-Holstein, upstream of the river mouth at Cuxhaven, and the town is defined by the Kiel Canal, the Nord-Ostsee-Kanal, whose western locks sit beside it. Ships moving between the North Sea and the Baltic lock in here, while others call at the port for cargo. The port facilities, run by Brunsbüttel Ports, are the Elbehafen, a tidal multi-purpose and bulk port on the river outside the locks, and two harbours on the canal itself, the oil harbour and the Ostermoor harbour. Behind them stretches the ChemCoast Park, the largest industrial area in Schleswig-Holstein, home to chemical, fertiliser, petroleum and energy companies whose raw materials and products move by ship.

The canal locks consist of large and small chambers, and an additional large chamber has been under construction so the canal can stay open while the older chambers are renewed. Ships arriving for the canal wait at the Elbe anchorages off Brunsbüttel when no lock is free, and canal pilots, with helmsmen on larger ships, join for the passage east. The Elbehafen handles liquid and dry bulk, general cargo and project shipments for the industrial park, and since 2023 it has also hosted the floating storage and regasification unit Höegh Gannet at a temporary berth, while a purpose-built jetty is built on the western side of the harbour. That brings LNG carriers to Brunsbüttel alongside the tankers, bulk carriers and multipurpose ships that make up the regular traffic.

From an inspection point of view, Brunsbüttel combines an industrial tanker port with a transit point. The ships that actually stop, tankers at the oil and Ostermoor harbours, bulk carriers and multipurpose ships at the Elbehafen, stay for a cargo operation and can be gauged within it. Ships simply transiting the canal do not usually stop long enough for meaningful work unless the owner arranges a lay-by. Winter adds a northern element: the canal leads to the Baltic, where ice class matters, and in very cold spells ice can form on the canal and the lower Elbe and slow the traffic. Strong winds and the Elbe tide govern the timing of arrivals at the river berths, while the canal harbours behind the locks are free of tide.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged at Brunsbüttel
p: Brunsbüttel has no merchant ship dry dock, so gauging is carried out afloat during cargo operations or on lay-by. At the Elbehafen, bulk carriers give a hold window after discharge, multipurpose ships give tween-deck and hatch access between lifts, and tankers can have ballast tanks, decks and engine-room piping measured while cargo is handled under the terminal's rules. At the oil and Ostermoor harbours on the canal, chemical and product tankers follow the same pattern, with cargo tanks entered only once they are gas-freed.

LNG carriers discharging to the regasification unit operate under strict gas-safety arrangements, so any work aboard them is confined to spaces well away from the cargo system and has to be agreed with both the ship and the terminal operator. For dockings, ships go to the Hamburg yards up the Elbe, to Bremerhaven, or to Baltic yards reached through the canal, and thickness data taken at Brunsbüttel can serve as the yard's steel estimate. Ships that need a longer stop can be laid by at a berth arranged through the agent and the port.
list: Elbehafen bulk berths — hold, hopper and tank-top gauging on bulk carriers after discharge.
Elbehafen multi-purpose quay — tween-deck, hatch cover and crane pedestal checks on project and general cargo ships.
Elbehafen liquid berths — ballast tank, deck and engine-room readings on tankers within terminal rules.
Oil harbour on the canal — chemical and product tanker gauging of ballast tanks and deck piping.
Ostermoor harbour on the canal — work on tankers and bulk ships serving the industrial park.
Yards in Hamburg, Bremerhaven and the Baltic — the usual docking destinations, using Brunsbüttel readings for steel planning.

context.h: Port state control, ice class and energy trades at Brunsbüttel
p: Port state control at Brunsbüttel is a Paris MoU matter, carried out by BG Verkehr's Ship Safety Division, and the Kiel Canal adds its own traffic rules, administered by the federal waterways authority, for ships in transit. Many ships passing through are bound for Baltic ports where winter ice is normal, and those trading into the northern Baltic carry ice class under the Finnish-Swedish rules. Ice-belt plating at the bow and waterline wears faster than the rest of the shell, and owners preparing a ship for a winter of Baltic trading often want the ice belt, the bow and the frames behind it measured before the season starts.

Energy is the other theme. The regasification unit at the Elbehafen is part of Germany's LNG import system, operated by the state-owned Deutsche Energy Terminal, and an onshore LNG terminal is planned for the site, so LNG carriers have become regular callers. Chemical and fertiliser plants in the ChemCoast Park bring chemical tankers, gas carriers and bulk carriers. For all of them, EU ETS (from 2024) and FuelEU Maritime (from 2025) now reach voyages into the EU, and the EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires each of these ships to keep an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on board while calling here.

jobs.p: Brunsbüttel jobs are built around cargo calls at the Elbehafen and the canal harbours rather than around transits. A tanker loading or discharging gives a window for ballast tanks, deck structure and piping outside the cargo system; a bulk carrier gives one for holds after discharge; a multipurpose ship gives tween decks and hatches. Ships preparing for a Baltic winter add ice-belt work. The superintendent sets the scope before the team leaves India, the agent arranges terminal access, and results are sent before the ship sails into the canal or back down the Elbe, with the most critical findings flagged first. Typical requests:
list: A chemical tanker at the oil harbour: ballast tank and double-bottom gauging, deck plating and deck cargo-line wall thickness.
A bulk carrier after discharge at the Elbehafen: hold frames, brackets, hopper plating and tank top, ahead of its intermediate survey.
An ice-class general cargo ship before the Baltic winter: ice-belt shell plating, bow structure and the frames behind the ice belt.
A multipurpose ship loading project cargo for the industrial park: tween-deck pontoons, hatch covers and crane pedestal welds checked by magnetic particle testing.
A product tanker laid by after cleaning: cargo tank structure gauging for a pre-purchase inspection.

logistics: Hamburg Airport is the nearest international airport, and the team reaches Brunsbüttel by road along the north side of the Elbe; the Glückstadt to Wischhafen car ferry links the area with the Lower Saxony shore when a trip combines Brunsbüttel with Stade or Cuxhaven. Terminal access at the Elbehafen and the canal harbours is ISPS-controlled and arranged by the ship's agent, with extra safety induction at the chemical and LNG berths. The technicians from India travel on Schengen visas, so expected call dates should reach us early.

faqs.q: Can a ship be gauged while it waits for the Kiel Canal locks?
faqs.a: Rarely in any useful way. Waiting times for the locks are usually short and hard to predict, and boarding from a launch in the Elbe current is only practical for a very small scope. If an owner wants work done at Brunsbüttel, it is better to plan it into a cargo call at the Elbehafen or the canal harbours, or to arrange a lay-by berth through the agent.

faqs.q: Should ice-belt plating be gauged before a Baltic winter?
faqs.a: For ships trading into the northern Baltic, yes. The ice belt at the bow and along the waterline takes abrasion and impact loads, and coatings there wear away quickly, so thinning and local denting show up first in that band. Measuring the ice-belt plating and the frames behind it before the season gives the owner time to plan renewal or reinforcement at the next docking.

faqs.q: Is there a dry dock at Brunsbüttel?
faqs.a: There is no merchant ship dry dock at the port. Ships usually dock in Hamburg, in Bremerhaven, or at Baltic yards reached through the canal, depending on the owner's choice. Thickness data taken during a Brunsbüttel cargo call can be sent to that yard as a steel estimate, and our team can follow the ship to complete the programme in dock.

faqs.q: What can be done on a tanker at the oil harbour or the Ostermoor harbour?
faqs.a: Within the terminal's and the ship's safety rules, the spaces outside the cargo system can be gauged: ballast tanks, double bottom, deck plating, deck piping and the engine room. Cargo tanks need a gas-free certificate, which is unusual during a cargo call, so cargo-tank gauging is normally left for a lay-by after cleaning or for a docking.
